findings.title: Streaming rich Markdown re-splits a closed fenced code block at an internal blank line
findings.classification: formal static source finding; no dynamic parse/render observation
findings.ordinaryTrigger: The throttledText contains this ordinary assistant text while done=false and streamingRichRender remains its default true.
findings.contract: The source declares every chunk a self-contained block group including closed code blocks, and the leaf explicitly avoids dividing fenced blocks. Ordinary assistant text can contain a closed code block with an internal blank line and more prose still streaming.
findings.cause: The leaf fence-aware safe split is followed by unconditional prefix.split(/\n{2,}/).map(trim), with no fence context. Every result becomes a separate Markdown document.

staticCase.condition: The throttledText contains this ordinary assistant text while done=false and streamingRichRender remains its default true.
staticCase.derivation: splitStreamingMarkdown retains the closed fence as one stable prefix; splitIntoChunks then splits its internal blank line, trims, and invokes one independent StreamMarkdownChunk/ReactMarkdown per fragment.

producerAnchors.meaning: Normal stream start creates done:false; text_delta appends original text without sanitizing/removing code-block blank lines.
Nonempty ordinary assistant text and done flag forwarded; rich streaming is not disabled.

consumerAnchors.meaning: Closed fence with internal blank line stays wholly in stablePrefix when following prose is active tail.
Default rich stream uses chunker and one ReactMarkdown per chunk; done:true forwards full text directly to Markdown and bypasses chunker.

findings.impact: During rich streaming only, one complete fenced code block is fed as two incomplete independent Markdown fragments, so code-block structure is not preserved. Final done rendering bypasses the split and can restore the complete block. This helper does not change stored message text, files or clipboard; stream code-copy controls are intentionally absent.
counterevidence: No internal blank line means this particular split does not bisect the closed block. A still-open fence remains activeTail plain text, which is a different protected path.
done:true immediately forwards original complete text to Markdown; streamingRichRender:false is a full raw-pre fallback. This is not a final/persisted content-loss claim.

A response that completes before the affected rich-stream frame need not show the issue; ordinary longer responses can remain done:false after closing a block. No actual throttle timing or UI was measured.
The known C2 reference links/footnotes issue and R19 prompt fixed-fence family are separate and not re-counted.
